parsedVerdict.reasoning:
ListProjectTasksUseCase.execute does what an application layer should do. It checks that the project exists through the domain ProjectRepository port. It queries tasks through the domain TaskRepository port with the input filters. It maps the domain Task entities to TaskOutput DTOs in toOutput. The file has no persistence, SQL, framework or HTTP-handling logic, and no core business rules: the task status comes from task.getStatus() on the domain entity.

One minor concern: execute throws ApplicationError("project not found", 404), and 404 is an HTTP status code. That puts a bit of transport wording into the application layer. It is a common convention, though. The use case only reports a not-found outcome and does no HTTP handling itself, so I don't count it as a misplaced responsibility. That call is why confidence is moderate.
